evidence.notes: SObject.get accepts a Schema.SObjectField token and reads the stored field value.
SObject.put accepts a Schema.SObjectField token, writes the field value, and returns the previous value.
SObject.isSet accepts a Schema.SObjectField token and reports field presence.
SObject.putSObject accepts a reference field token and stores the parent relationship SObject.

source.content: @isTest private class DataRuntimeSObjectFieldTokenAccessTest { @isTest static void fieldTokenGetPutAndIsSet() { Schema.SObjectField nameField = Account.SObjectType.getDescribe().fields.getMap().get('Name'); Account account = new Account(); System.assertEquals(false, account.isSet(nameField)); System.assertEquals(null, account.get(nameField)); Object previous = account.put(nameField, 'Acme'); System.assertEquals(null, previous); System.assertEquals(true, account.isSet(nameField)); System.assertEquals('Acme', account.get(nameField)); previous = account.put(nameField, 'Changed'); System.assertEquals('Acme', previous); System.assertEquals('Changed', account.Name); } @isTest static void fieldTokenPutSObjectStoresParentRelationship() { Schema.SObjectField accountField = Contact.SObjectType.getDescribe().fields.getMap().get('AccountId'); Contact contact = new Contact(LastName = 'Child'); contact.putSObject(accountField, new Account(Id = '001000000000001AAA', Name = 'Parent')); System.assertEquals('Parent', contact.getSObject(accountField).get('Name')); } }
